title: Rapid Reassurance Playbook — weekend-mode comms scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for crafting short-form internal comms during a weekend/after-hours service disruption. This is NOT the formal ops runbook — think: what to say fast, where to post, who to ping, and a tiny Q&A crib for leadership and product PMs that will inevitably ask for a timeline.

Audience:
- Primary: SRE oncall, who needs one-line slack + status templates
- Secondary: Eng leads and PMs who will be copied on comms and want a short blurb
- Tertiary: Execs (very short summary + impact)

TL;DR (what to hit in first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm scope & impact: which regions/customers affected (if unknown, say: under investigation, targeted customers being triaged).
2) Post short initial Slack in #sre-oncall and #platform-incidents with link to incident stub.
3) Create/hand off status page entry (minimal: title, impact, eta placeholder).
4) Notify CS/Support lead (DM + brief) so they can prepare customer-facing replies.

Initial Slack template (post in #sre-oncall and #platform-incidents):
- SUBJECT: [URGENT] Serving latency spike — investigating
- BODY: Hey all — seeing elevated inference latencies in prod (primary: us-west1, maybe eu-west). Error rates up ~4x on model-route /v1/generate for the last 8m. Oncall investigating; creating incident OPS-1729. Will update in 15 mins. If you see customer reports, DM me.

Status page minimal entry (status.redwood.ai):
- Title: Elevated inference latency for hosted API
- Impact: Intermittent increased latency and 5xxs for text generation routes affecting a subset of customers in US-WEST and EU-WEST
- Started: 2026-03-12T02:18Z
- Update: Investigating — updates every 30 minutes
- Contact: support@redwood.ai (for customers)

Short exec blurb (for CEO/GM):
- One-liner: We’re experiencing intermittent elevated latencies on hosted text generation in two regions; root cause under investigation; mitigation work in progress.
- Current impact: ~2–6% of requests degraded, spike correlates to a rollout of a new batching config on dedicated hosts (hypothesis).
- Next step: rollback config on canaries, validate, and widen if stable. ETA for next update: 30m.

All-hands talking points (if asked to repeat):
- We have an active incident; SRE + Serving runtime leads are on it. Our priority is to keep customer-facing latency and 5xxs minimized and restore normal traffic patterns.
- We have fallbacks in place (model routing to compatible variants) and are evaluating traffic-steering to reduce load on affected pools.
- No data loss reported, all user data paths intact.

Rapid Q&A crib (expected questions & short answers):
Q: Is this customer impacting?
A: Yes — some customers may see slower responses and occasional errors; we’re prioritizing the highest-volume tenants and payment-related routes.

Q: Do we have a rollback plan?
A: Yes — the immediate rollback candidate is the recent batching/queue config pushed to canaries. If canary rollback reverses the spike, we’ll proceed to affected pools.

Q: How long until normal?
A: Early estimate 1–3 hours depending on rollback validation or routing changes. Will update every 30 minutes.

Monitoring & quick checks (what I run first):
- Grafana: request latency + 5xx rate by route and region (prod > us-west1, eu-west)
- Infra: GPU utilization and queue length on dedicated pools
- Serving runtime logs: increase in backlog warnings, kv-cache misses, or kernel OOMs
- Recent deploys/rollouts: check last 2 hours for canary/batch config changes (CI/CD logs)

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
1) Oncall SRE (primary) — initial triage (me)
2) Serving runtime lead — Dmitri Kovalenko (DM + call if need infra-level change)
3) Platform eng lead — Marta Lopez (for routing/traffic policy overrides)
4) Product EM for hosted API — Ravi Patel (customer comms + priorities)
5) CEO — only if >2 hours or major customer outage (prepare one-liner)

Customer comms short FAQ (for CS):
- Short answer: We’re aware of elevated latencies for text generation in US-WEST and EU-WEST; engineers are actively investigating; no data loss; next update in 30 minutes.
- If a customer asks for workaround: suggest switching to a compatible lower-latency model variant or pinning to dedicated capacity (if available).

Post-incident notes to capture (quick checklist for retrospective):
- Timeline of events with Timestamps (first spike, mitigation steps, rollback, resolution)
- Root cause analysis hypothesis + data to confirm (e.g., rollout ID, config diff)
- Customer impact table: affected tenants, duration, support actions taken
- Action items: telemetry gaps, automation to detect similar regressions, runbook improvements

My live scratch items (things I still need while drafting final comms):
- [ ] Confirm whether a canary rollback was performed automatically by deployment pipeline (CI job logs)
- [ ] Get raw percent of requests affected from metrics (need query from grafana)
- [ ] Draft short customer-facing note for CS (1–2 lines + suggestion)
- [ ] Confirm if any scheduled jobs coincided with the spike (cron/ETL)

Tone notes (for public/internal message):
- Internal: transparent + specific; name the impacted regions and affected routes if we know them; include next update ETA.
- External/customer-facing: concise, empathic, and actionable (workaround + contact).

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Did any autoscaling events coincide with the spike?
- Are kv-cache eviction rates abnormal during the window?
- Any kernel OOM logs in the serving runtime tenants?

Versioning & provenance (for the eventual postmortem):
- Save the incident stub ID (OPS-1729) and link to timeline notes in Confluence.
- Snapshot key dashboards and attach to postmortem.

Notes-to-self (personal):
- Keep initial comms short (one sentence) — the team needs to act, not read an essay.
- Avoid speculative root cause in early comms. Use hypothesis language ("investigating potential link to X").

----
End scratchpad. Use as a base for the incident channel starter and for the short CS note. Will copy into incident ticket and fill exact numbers once graphed.
